definitions.explanation: Administrative suffix used for Osaka and Kyoto prefectures.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大阪|おおさか}→大阪：09779_oosaka⟧{府|ふ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{住|す}んでいる→住む：00673_sumu⟧。
⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧{府|ふ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{場所|ばしょ}→場所：00829_basho⟧だ。
examples.english: Kyoto Prefecture is a place with history.

examples.japanese: {府|ふ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{県|けん}→県：02151_ken⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{違|ちが}い→違い：03432_chigai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{歴史的|れきしてき}→歴史的：05671_rekishiteki⟧なものだ。
examples.english: The difference between fu and ken is historical.

notes:
{府|ふ} is an administrative designation for urban prefectures in Japan.

USAGE:
Only two prefectures use {府|ふ}:
- ⟦{大阪|おおさか}→大阪：09779_oosaka⟧{府|ふ} (Osaka)
- ⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧{府|ふ} (Kyoto)

JAPANESE PREFECTURAL DIVISIONS:
- {都|と}: Tokyo only ({東京都|とうきょうと})
- {道|どう}: Hokkaido only (⟦{北海道|ほっかいどう}→北海道：11010_hokkaidou⟧)
- {府|ふ}: Osaka, Kyoto
- ⟦{県|けん}→県：02151_ken⟧: All other 43 prefectures

ETYMOLOGY:
The {府|ふ} designation dates from the Meiji period when these cities served as major urban centers. There were originally more {府|ふ} designations, but most were changed to ⟦{県|けん}→県：02151_ken⟧.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{県|けん}→県：02151_ken⟧: prefecture (most common)
- ⟦{知事|ちじ}→知事：03467_chiji⟧: prefectural governor
- {府民|ふみん}: residents of Osaka/Kyoto Prefecture
